addr_t ext_dma_req_q_addr_nontrunc;

claims.finding: A copy has one local L1 address leg and one host-side external address leg; do not count both copy addresses as two translated requests.

All examined external RX/RY AR and WY AW have the same stream_id=0, ss_id_valid=1, substream_id=0. The wiring supplies no two independent context identities. InclPC=0/InclBC=0 are recorded parameters; internal feature semantics and programmed context state are not newly audited.

Separate AR/AW FIFOs and independent VALID/READY emitters, plus inherited serialize=0, do not impose a whole-job completion barrier. Cross-copy external read/write address work is structurally possible under pipeline/resource/routing conditions, but no end-to-end reachability or dual-admission execution certificate is provided.
No actual simultaneous external request occupancy, IOMMU dual acceptance, arbitration conflict, HOL, latency propagation, or net performance follows from these sources or their FIFO depths.

For RX/RY, remote R acceptance/completion and the local TCDM write B retirement are separate protocol events. Fixed native job completion follows final write B, so remote R alone cannot certify input readiness for the L1 consumer. No nonzero natural timing gap is observed.

claims.finding: Native AW ID0 is inherited. Input AW targets local TCDMDMA and output AW targets external SoCDMAOut. DMA xbar has UniqueIds=0, references the package WideIdWidthIn parameter, and has configured outstanding limits4; this decision does not rely on the concrete package ID width. The actual same-ID cross-destination ordering implementation may restrict WY external AW visibility until prior local writes release a destination constraint; implementation was not read. Do not assert external WY AW is visible merely because its whole descriptor was accepted.

A condition-only positive/adjacent-negative protocol cut can share an accepted descriptor prefix while differing in input-local-B completed prefix and both retaining an unretired old output. This report supports neither identical complete IOMMU observations nor natural/default-cycle reachability, and imposes no identical external AW handshake prefix. Root owns case construction and acceptance.
